title: Halting and Reachability Decision
statement: Let $E$ be a natural number with $1\le E$, let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $\mathrm{orc}$ assign a Boolean answer to each of four query types and each Boolean word. Suppose that for every natural number $k\le |x|$, the answer to query type $0$ on the encoding of $x$ and the binary word for $k$ is true exactly when $k<|x|$. The register program, started in its scan state with all registers zero and no answer, halts with the Boolean value of the following proposition: there are $u,v<2^{(|x|+2)^{2E}}$ such that query type $1$ accepts $u$ as an initial code and query type $2$ accepts $v$ as an accepting code, both at radius $(|x|+2)^E$, and $u$ reaches $v$ in $(|x|+2)^{2E}$ levels under the relation specified by query type $3$ at that radius, with intermediate codes bounded by $2^{(|x|+2)^{2E}}$. Throughout the run, every register value is at most $2^{((|x|+2)^{2E})((|x|+2)^{2E})}$.
